seo.title: How Much Do Barbershop Owners Make in the UK? A Model P&L
seo.description: A transparent UK model of what barbershop owners earn at two, four and six chairs, and the three cost lines that decide whether the shop pays its owner.

media.anchor: # What Does a UK Barbershop Owner Actually Earn? A Model Profit and Loss, Chair by Chair
media.alt: Red barber chair and grooming workstations in a real London salon interior
media.caption: A grooming salon interior photographed in London. Editorial illustration only — the premises are not KERSIVO customers or the invented shops in the model
media.rights: Original Pexels photo #9703068 by Jennifer Latham, source https://www.pexels.com/photo/red-armchair-at-hairdresser-9703068/, with London, England, United Kingdom location and Free to use licence https://www.pexels.com/license/ permitting commercial editorial blog display/crops. Photo ID audited against all 17 production Insights manifests on 19 Oct 2026: unique. Subject premises/brands/people not endorsed by or associated with KERSIVO, with no claims of their finances.

media.anchor: A shop making £180,000 in annual sales does not have £180,000 to distribute.
media.alt: Two hypothetical four-chair UK shops each have 180000 pounds turnover; Shop A has 85342 pounds operating profit and 52810 pounds cash left, versus Shop B with 43937 pounds profit and 21781 pounds cash
media.caption: Same hypothetical £180,000 turnover, different costs. Cash figures follow estimated sole-trader tax, loan principal repayments and equipment cash spend
media.rights: Original KERSIVO vector chart based on original Notion IDEA-011 validated model, independently recalculated to unrounded £85,341.60 vs £43,936.60 operating profit and £52,809.53 vs £21,781.28 after the stated tax and cash assumptions. Illustrative, not national statistics or actual client data.

media.anchor: The difference between the rows looks attractive
media.alt: Hypothetical contribution before fixed overhead for working owner plus employed barbers: two chairs 66247 pounds, four chairs 114142 pounds, six chairs 162036 pounds
media.caption: Before rent, rates, utilities, equipment, other fixed overhead and personal tax; scaling chairs requires matching demand, space and staffing
media.rights: Original KERSIVO vector chart. Model: owner-chair £45,000 revenue, 2% fees and 4% consumables, equals £42,300 contribution. Each employee adds £45,000 revenue less £18,000 pay, £352.80 employer pension, £900 fees, £1,800 consumables = £23,947.20. Calculations: 2 chairs £66,247.20; 4 £114,141.60; 6 £162,036.00. Employment Allowance assumed eligible. These are not owner income figures.
